title: HTTP/2, HTTP/3 & Desync
description: Protocol-level request parsing, stream handling, and proxy/backend disagreements.

attacks.name: H2C smuggling
attacks.notes: Upgrade: h2c header diye frontend bypass
attacks.desc: An h2c upgrade can create a parsing gap when a proxy and backend disagree on how the upgraded request is handled.
attacks.prevention: Disable h2c upgrades where not required, and ensure the front end and backend agree on upgrade routing and authentication.

attacks.name: H2.CL desync
attacks.desc: A front end and backend may disagree about HTTP/2 body length when Content-Length is translated or checked differently.
attacks.prevention: Patch and align HTTP/2 gateways so Content-Length and body framing are validated before translation to HTTP/1.1.

attacks.name: H2.TE desync
attacks.desc: Transfer-Encoding handling across an HTTP/2 gateway can desynchronize requests if the backend interprets the body differently.
attacks.prevention: Reject forbidden or ambiguous transfer headers in HTTP/2 requests and keep gateway parsers updated.

attacks.name: CL.TE / TE.CL / TE.TE
attacks.desc: Conflicting message-length headers can cause a proxy and backend to assign bytes to different HTTP requests.
attacks.prevention: Use consistent message-length parsing across proxies and origins, reject conflicting headers, and patch affected components.

attacks.name: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset
attacks.desc: Rapid HTTP/2 stream cancellation can consume server resources faster than they are released.

attacks.name: HPACK bomb
attacks.desc: A small HPACK header block can expand into large headers and exhaust decoder memory or CPU.

attacks.name: Request tunnelling
attacks.desc: A crafted request can carry another request through a proxy when framing rules differ between layers.

attacks.name: HTTP/3 / QUIC probes
attacks.desc: QUIC and HTTP/3 endpoints may expose services or policy differences that are absent on TCP-based HTTP.

attacks.name: Client-side desync
attacks.desc: Browser-initiated requests can desynchronize a connection when the server leaves bytes for a subsequent request.

attacks.name: Connection state desync
attacks.desc: Reused connections can carry stale parser state, allowing one request to affect how the next is interpreted.
